papers.name: Components 1 and 2 (all content; Component 1 non-calculator, Component 2 calculator)

topics.name: Number
points: HN1 Order positive and negative integers, decimals and fractions; use the symbols =, ≠, <, >, ≤, ≥
HN2 Apply the four operations, including formal written methods, to integers, decimals, simple fractions and mixed numbers; place value
HN3 Relationships between operations including inverse operations; priority of operations including brackets, powers, roots and reciprocals
HN4 Prime numbers, factors, multiples, HCF, LCM, prime factorisation and the unique factorisation theorem
HN5 Systematic listing strategies, including the product rule for counting
HN6 Positive integer powers and real roots; recognise powers of 2, 3, 4, 5; estimate powers and roots
HN7 Calculate with roots and with integer and fractional indices
HN8 Calculate exactly with fractions, surds and multiples of π; simplify surds and rationalise denominators
HN9 Calculate with and interpret standard form A × 10ⁿ
HN10 Change recurring decimals into fractions and vice versa; terminating decimals
HN11 Identify and work with fractions in ratio problems
HN12 Interpret fractions and percentages as operators
HN13 Standard units and compound measures, using decimal quantities
HN14 Estimate answers and check calculations, including those obtained using technology
HN15 Round to an appropriate degree of accuracy; use inequality notation for error intervals
HN16 Apply and interpret limits of accuracy, including upper and lower bounds

topics.name: Algebra
points: HA1 Use and interpret algebraic notation, including indices, fractional coefficients and brackets
HA2 Substitute numerical values into formulae and expressions, including scientific formulae
HA3 Vocabulary of expressions, equations, formulae, identities, inequalities, terms and factors
HA4 Simplify and manipulate expressions including surds and algebraic fractions; factorise quadratics; complete the square
HA5 Use standard formulae and rearrange formulae to change the subject
HA6 Distinguish equations and identities; argue mathematically and construct algebraic proofs
HA7 Interpret expressions as functions; inverse and composite functions
HA8 Work with coordinates in all four quadrants
HA9 Straight-line graphs; y = mx + c; parallel and perpendicular lines; find equations of lines
HA10 Identify and interpret gradients and intercepts of linear functions graphically and algebraically
HA11 Roots, intercepts and turning points of quadratics; deduce roots and turning points algebraically (completing the square)
HA12 Recognise, sketch and interpret linear, quadratic, cubic, reciprocal, exponential and trigonometric graphs
HA13 Sketch translations and reflections of a given function
HA14 Plot and interpret reciprocal, exponential and non-standard graphs in real contexts
HA15 Calculate or estimate gradients of graphs and areas under graphs; interpret in context
HA16 Equation of a circle with centre at the origin; equation of a tangent at a given point
HA17 Solve linear equations in one unknown algebraically; approximate solutions graphically
HA18 Solve quadratic equations by factorising, completing the square and the quadratic formula; approximate from graphs
HA19 Solve simultaneous equations (linear/linear and linear/quadratic) algebraically; approximate from graphs
HA20 Approximate solutions to equations numerically using iteration
HA21 Translate situations into equations, solve them and interpret the solution
HA22 Solve linear and quadratic inequalities; represent solution sets on number lines, graphs and in set notation
HA23 Generate terms of a sequence from term-to-term or position-to-term rules
HA24 Recognise and use triangular, square, cube, Fibonacci-type, quadratic and geometric sequences and other sequences
HA25 Deduce expressions for the nth term of linear and quadratic sequences

topics.name: Ratio, proportion and rates of change
points: HR1 Change between related standard units and compound units in numerical and algebraic contexts
HR2 Density and pressure and their relationships with mass, volume, force and area
HR3 Use scale factors, scale diagrams and maps
HR4 Express one quantity as a fraction of another, where the fraction is less than or greater than 1
HR5 Use ratio notation, including reduction to simplest form
HR6 Divide a quantity into parts in a given ratio; apply ratio to real contexts (conversion, scaling, mixing)
HR7 Express a multiplicative relationship between two quantities as a ratio or a fraction
HR8 Understand and use proportion as equality of ratios
HR9 Relate ratios to fractions and to linear functions
HR10 Percentages: percentage change, original value, simple interest, percentages over 100%
HR11 Solve problems involving direct and inverse proportion, including graphical and algebraic representations
HR12 Use compound units such as speed, rates of pay, unit pricing, density and pressure
HR13 Compare lengths, areas and volumes using ratio notation; scale factors and similarity
HR14 Inverse proportion as proportionality to 1/Y; construct and interpret equations describing direct and inverse proportion
HR15 Interpret the gradient of a straight line graph as a rate of change; direct and inverse proportion graphs
HR16 Gradient at a point on a curve as the instantaneous rate of change; average and instantaneous rates of change
HR17 Growth and decay problems, including compound interest and general iterative processes

topics.name: Geometry and measures
points: HG1 Conventional terms and notation; labelling triangles; drawing diagrams from written descriptions
HG2 Ruler and compass constructions and loci; perpendicular distance as shortest distance
HG3 Angle facts at a point, on a line, vertically opposite, parallel lines; angle sums of triangles and polygons
HG4 Properties and definitions of special triangles, quadrilaterals and other plane figures
HG5 Congruence criteria SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS
HG6 Derive results about angles and sides using Pythagoras and isosceles triangles; simple proofs
HG7 Congruent and similar shapes using transformations, including fractional and negative scale factors
HG8 Changes and invariance achieved by combinations of rotations, reflections and translations
HG9 Circle definitions and properties: centre, radius, chord, diameter, circumference, tangent, arc, sector, segment
HG10 Apply and prove the standard circle theorems
HG11 Solve geometrical problems on coordinate axes
HG12 Faces, surfaces, edges and vertices of cubes, prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres
HG13 Construct and interpret plans and elevations of 3D shapes
HG14 Standard units of measure and related concepts (length, area, volume, angle, mass, time, money)
HG15 Measure lines and angles; maps, scale drawings and bearings
HG16 Area of triangles, parallelograms and trapezia; volume of cuboids, right prisms and cylinders
HG17 Circumference and area of circles; surface area and volume of spheres, pyramids, cones and composite solids
HG18 Arc lengths, angles and areas of sectors
HG19 Similarity: relationships between lengths, areas and volumes in similar figures
HG20 Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometric ratios in 2D and 3D triangles
HG21 Exact values of sin, cos and tan for 0°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 90°
HG22 Sine and cosine rules to find unknown lengths and angles
HG23 Area of a triangle = ½ab sin C
HG24 Describe translations as 2D vectors
HG25 Vector arithmetic; use vectors to construct geometric arguments and proofs

topics.name: Probability
points: HP1 Record, describe and analyse frequencies of outcomes using tables and frequency trees
HP2 Apply ideas of randomness, fairness and equally likely events to calculate expected outcomes
HP3 Relate relative expected frequencies to theoretical probability on the 0–1 scale
HP4 Probabilities of an exhaustive set of outcomes sum to one
HP5 Empirical unbiased samples tend towards theoretical probability with increasing sample size
HP6 Enumerate sets and combinations of sets systematically using tables, grids, Venn diagrams and tree diagrams
HP7 Construct theoretical possibility spaces for single and combined experiments
HP8 Probability of independent and dependent combined events using tree diagrams
HP9 Conditional probability using expected frequencies, two-way tables, tree diagrams and Venn diagrams

topics.name: Statistics
points: HS1 Infer properties of populations from samples; limitations of sampling
HS2 Design and criticise questions for a questionnaire, including fairness
HS3 Construct and interpret tables, charts and diagrams for categorical, discrete and time series data
HS4 Histograms with equal and unequal class intervals; cumulative frequency graphs
HS5 Compare distributions using graphs including box plots, averages, range, quartiles and interquartile range
HS6 Apply statistics to describe a population
HS7 Scatter graphs: correlation, lines of best fit, predictions and dangers of extrapolation
